Loss of $KE =$ Gain in $PE$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2} = mgh \left(\dfrac{R}{h + R}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{{h}_{1}}{{h}_{1} + R}$

Solving (ii)

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{{h}_{2}}{{h}_{2} + R}$ ...(iv)

$⇒ {h}_{2} = 2R$

From (iii) and (iv)

$⇒ \dfrac{{h}_{1}}{{h}_{2}} = \dfrac{R / 2}{2R}$

$∴ \dfrac{{h}_{1}}{{h}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{4} = 0 . 25$

decrease in $KE =$ increase in GPE

${M}_{A} = \sigma4\pi{R}_A^{2}, {M}_{B} = \sigma4\pi{R}_B^{2}$

where $\sigma$ is surface density

${V}_{A} = \dfrac{- G{M}_{A}}{{R}_{A}}, {V}_{B} = \dfrac{- G{M}_{B}}{{R}_{B}}$

questions.q: A large sphere of mass $M$ is fixed at one position and two identical particles each of mass $m$ are kept on a line passing through the centre of $M$ (see figure). The point masses are connected by a rigid massless rod of length $l$ and this assembly is free to move along the line connecting them. All three masses interact only through their mutual gravitational interaction. When the point mass nearer to $M$ is at a distance $r = 3l$ from $M$, the tension in the rod is zero for $m = k\left(\dfrac{M}{288}\right)$. The value of $k$ is
questions.solution:
Due to gravitational interaction connected masses have some acceleration.

Let both small masses are moving with acceleration 'a' towards larger mass M



Force equation for mass nearer to a larger mass

$\dfrac{GMm}{{\left(3l\right)}^{2}} - \dfrac{G{m}^{2}}{{l}^{2}} = ma$ ...(i)

Force equation for mass away from a larger mass

$\dfrac{GMm}{{\left(4l\right)}^{2}} + \dfrac{G{m}^{2}}{{l}^{2}} = ma$ ...(ii)

From equation (i) & (ii)

$\dfrac{GM}{9{l}^{2}} - \dfrac{Gm}{{l}^{2}} = \dfrac{GM}{16{l}^{2}} + \dfrac{Gm}{{l}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{M}{9} - \dfrac{M}{16} = m + m$

$\dfrac{7M}{144} = 2m$

$⇒ m = \dfrac{7M}{288} = k\left(\dfrac{M}{288}\right)$

$⇒ k = 7$

questions.q: Suppose the gravitational force varies inversely as the $n^{th}$ power of the distance. Then the time period of a planet in circular orbit of radius $R$& around the sun will be proportional to
questions.solution:
Gravitational force $= \dfrac{GMm}{d^{2}}$ (Newton's law)

But in this case, $F = \dfrac{GMm}{R^{n}}$ and it provides the necessary centripetal force $\dfrac{mv^{2}}{R}$

$∴\dfrac{mv^{2}}{R} = \dfrac{GMm}{R^{n}}$
$∴v = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{R^{n - 1}}}$ and the period $T$ of a planet, $T = \dfrac{2\piR}{v}$

questions.q:
A projectile of mass $m$ is fired from the surface of the earth at an angle $\alpha = 6 {0}^{∘}$ from the vertical. The initial speed ${v}_{0}$ is equal to $\sqrt{\dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}}}{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}}$. The maximum height that projectile can rise from the surface of the earth is $\dfrac{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{\text{x}}$. Find the value of $x$?

$G$ = Universal Gravitational constant
${M}_{e}$ = Mass of earth
${R}_{e}$ = Radius of earth
questions.solution:
By conservation of angular momentum about C at position P and F

${\text{mv}}_{0} \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} = \text{mv} {r}_{\text{max}}$

$⇒ \text{v} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} {\text{v}}_{0}}{2 {r}_{\text{max}}}$ ...(i)

By conservation of mechanical energy between P and F

$\dfrac{1}{2} {\text{mv}}_{0}^{2} - \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}} \text{m}}{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}} = \dfrac{1}{2} {\text{mv}}^{2} - \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}} \text{m}}{{\text{r}}_{\text{max}}}$ ...(ii)

Put (i) in (ii)

$\dfrac{1}{2} {\text{mv}}_{0}^{2} - \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}} \text{m}}{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \text{m} \dfrac{3 {\text{R}}^{2} {\text{v}}_{0}^{2}}{4 {r}_{\text{max}}^{2}} - \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}} \text{m}}{{\text{r}}_{\text{max}}}$

${\text{v}}_{0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}}}{\text{R}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} \text{m} \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}}}{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}} - \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}} \text{m}}{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}} = \dfrac{3}{8} \dfrac{{\text{mR}}_{\text{e}}^{2}}{{\text{r}}_{\text{max}}^{2}} \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}}}{\text{R}} - \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}} \text{m}}{{\text{r}}_{\text{max}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}} - \dfrac{1}{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}} = \dfrac{3 \text{R}}{8 {r}_{\text{max}}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{\text{r}}_{\text{max}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 1}{2 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}} = \dfrac{3 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} - 8 {r}_{\text{max}}}{8 {r}_{\text{max}}^{2}}$

$⇒ 4 {\text{r}}_{\text{max}}^{2} - 8 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} {r}_{\text{max}} + 3 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}^{2} = 0$

Solving the quadratic in rmax

we get

${\text{r}}_{\text{max}} = \dfrac{8 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} \pm \sqrt{1 6} {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{8} = \dfrac{8 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} \pm 4 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{8}$

$⇒ {\text{r}}_{\text{max}} = \dfrac{8 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} + 4 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{8} = \dfrac{1 2 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{8} = \dfrac{3 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{2}$

$∴ {\text{h}}_{\text{max}} = {\text{r}}_{\text{max}} - {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} = \dfrac{3 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{2} - {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} = \dfrac{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{2}$

$∴ \text{x} = 2$

questions.q: A body hanging from a massless spring stretches it by $3$ cm on earth's surface. At a place $800$ km above the earth's surface, the same body will stretch the spring by (Radius of Earth $= 6400km$)
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity,

$g = \dfrac{GM}{r^{2}}$

$∴ g ∝ \dfrac{1}{r^{2}}$

When the body is hanged on a spring

$F = - kx = mg$.....(i)

Acts on it, where $x$ is extension in spring. Let $800$ km above the Earth's surface, the stretch in the length of spring is $x′$ and value of $g$ is $g′$.

$g = \dfrac{GM}{R^{2}}$ and $g^{′} = \dfrac{GM}{{\left(R + h\right)}^{2}}$

So, $g^{′} = \dfrac{g}{{\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)}^{2}}$....(ii)

Where, $R =$ radius of Earth

From Equation (i), we get

$kx = mg⇒ x ∝ g$......(iii)

Therefore, $\dfrac{x′}{x} = \dfrac{g′}{g}

From Equations (ii) and (iii), we get

\dfrac{x′}{x} = \dfrac{\dfrac{g}{{\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)}^{2}}}{g} = \dfrac{g}{g{\left(1 + \dfrac{800 \times {10}^{3}}{6400 \times {10}^{3}}\right)}^{2}}$

$= \dfrac{g}{g{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{8}\right)}^{2}}$

$= \dfrac{g}{g{\left(\dfrac{9}{8}\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{g \times 64}{g \times 81} = \dfrac{64}{81}$

$x^{′} = \dfrac{64}{81}x \left[x = 3cm\right]$

$⇒ x^{′} = \dfrac{64}{81} \times3 = \dfrac{64}{27}$

$⇒ x^{′} = \dfrac{64}{27}$ cm$$

questions.q: If the escape speed of a projectile on Earth's surface is $11. 2kms^{- 2}$ and a body is projected out with thrice this speed, then determine the speed of the body far away from the Earth
questions.solution:
According to the principal of conservation of energy,

Initial kinetic energy + initial potential energy,

= final kinetic energy + final potential energy

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} - \dfrac{GMm}{R} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{′2} + 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{′2} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} - \dfrac{GMm}{R}$ ..... (i)

As consider, ${v}_{e} =$ escape velocity

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_e^{2} = \dfrac{GMm}{R}$ ........ (ii)

$∴$ From equation (i) and (ii), we get

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{′2} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_e^{2}$ ...... (iii)

$⇒ v^{′2} = v^{2} - {v}_e^{2}$

Now, $\left\begin{array}{ll}{v}_{e} = 11.2kms^{- 1} \\ v = 3{v}_{e}\end{array}$\right\}$ .... (iv)

From equation (iii) and (iv), we get

$v^{′2} = {$\left(3{v}_{e}\right)$}^{2} - {v}_e^{2}$

$v^{′2} = 9{v}_e^{2} - {v}_e^{2} = 8{v}_e^{2} = 8 \times {$\left(11.2\right)$}^{2}$

$= 8 \times {$\left(11.2\right)$}^{2}$

$⇒ v^{′} = \sqrt{8 \times {$\left(11.2\right)$}^{2}} = \sqrt{8} \times 11.2$

$v^{′} = 2 \times 1.414 \times 11.2 = 31.68kms^{- 1}$

$∴$ Speed of the body far away from the Earth,

$v ' = 31 . 68kms^{- 1} = 31 . 7kms^{- 1}

questions.q: How many time faster than the present speed would the earth have to rotate about its axis so that the apparent weight of the bodies on the equator becomes zero? (The radius of the earth $R = 6.4 \times {10}^{6}m$)
questions.solution:
Let ${\omega}_{0}$ be the new angular velocity.

At the equator ${g}_{E} = g - R{\omega}^{2}$

The weight $m{g}_{E}$ should be zero. ${g}_{E} = 0$

$∴ R{\omega}_{0}^{2} = g$ or ${\omega}_{0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{R}}$

$∴ {\omega}_{0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9.8}{6.4 \times 1{0}^{6}}} = 1.24 \times 1{0}^{- 3}\dfrac{rad}{s}$

The present angular velocity of the earth is $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} = \dfrac{2 \times 3.14}{24 \times 60 \times 60}$

$∴\omega = \dfrac{3.14 \times 1{0}^{- 2}}{12 \times 36} = 7.27 \times 1{0}^{- 5}$

$∴ \dfrac{{\omega}_{0}}{\omega} = \dfrac{1.24 \times 1{0}^{- 3}}{7.27 \times 1{0}^{- 5}} = 17$

$∴ {\omega}_{0} = 17\omega$

It should rotate faster by 17 times the present value.

$Since, {T}_{e} = 365days = 1year, wehave$

${T}_{p} = 2\sqrt{2} \times 365days$

${T}_{P} = 1032days$

questions.q: Gravitational acceleration on the surface of a planet is $\dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{11}g$ , where g is the gravitational acceleration on the surface of the earth. The average mass density of the planet is $\dfrac{2}{3}$ times that of the earth. If the escape speed on the surface of the earth is taken to be 11 km/s, the escape speed on the surface of the planet in km/s will be
questions.solution:
$g = \dfrac{GM}{R^{2}} = \dfrac{G}{R^{2}}\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}ρ = \dfrac{4}{3}\piGRρ$ i.e. $g ∝ Rρ$

$\dfrac{{g}_{P}}{{g}_{E}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}{g}_{E}}{11{g}_{E}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{11}$ and $\dfrac{{ρ}_{E}}{{ρ}_{P}} = \dfrac{3}{2}$ and $\dfrac{{g}_{P}}{{g}_{E}} = \dfrac{{R}_{P}{ρ}_{P}}{{R}_{E}{ρ}_{E}}$

$∴ \dfrac{{R}_{P}}{{R}_{E}} = \dfrac{{g}_{P}{ρ}_{E}}{{g}_{E}{ρ}_{P}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{11} \times \dfrac{3}{2}$

$∴$ Escape velocity $v = \sqrt{2gR}$

$∴ \dfrac{{v}_{P}}{{v}_{E}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{g}_{P}}{{g}_{E}} \times \dfrac{{R}_{P}}{{R}_{E}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{11} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{11} \times \dfrac{3}{2}}= \dfrac{3}{11}$

$∴ {v}_{P} = \dfrac{3}{11} \times {v}_{E} = \dfrac{3}{11} \times 11 = 3kms^{- 1}$

The sphere with the cavity now applies a gravitational force ${F}_{2}$ on the same particle placed at $P$.
The ratio $\dfrac{F2}{F1}$& will be
questions.solution:
Gravitational force due to solid sphere, ${F}_{1} = \dfrac{GMm}{\left(2\text{R}\right)2}$ where M and m are mass of the solid sphere and particle respectively and R is the radius of the sphere.

The gravitational force on the particle due to sphere with cavity = force due to a solid sphere - force due to sphere creating a cavity, assumed to be present above at that position.

i.e., ${F}_{2} = \dfrac{GMm}{4R^{2}} - \dfrac{\text{G}\left(\text{M} / 8\right)\text{m}}{\left(3\text{R} / 2\right)2} = \dfrac{7}{36}\dfrac{GMm}{\text{R}2}$

So $\dfrac{\text{F}2}{\text{F}1} = \dfrac{7\text{GMm}}{36R^{2}}\left(\dfrac{GMm}{4R^{2}}\right) = \dfrac{7}{9}$
